OpenElixir-02 1.3, custom firmware for the Erica Synths LXR-02 drum machine: a **step arp**, **faster
knobs**, **LFOs on the whole unit** and a reworked **pattern management** with names and patterns from
other projects.

> Tested on hardware by the author. OpenElixir-02 is not official Erica Synths firmware and is not
> affiliated with or approved by Erica Synths. Install it at your own risk.

## Step arp

Two new step parameters next to flam (`flm`) and shift (`shf`) on the step page:

- **`chd`**: Rep, Maj, Min, Dim, Aug, Maj7, Min7, Dim7, Aug7. Rep (the default) is the stock flam: every
  substep repeats the step's note.
- **`dir`**: Up or Dn.
- The flam setting chooses the number of notes. Maj with x4 and Up plays the step's note, +4, +7 and +12.
  With more notes than the chord has, it continues one octave higher; Dn plays the same notes in
  reverse.
- Arp notes keep the step's shift and go to MIDI out as well.

The arp is saved with the pattern. Patterns from the stock firmware and older versions load with Rep;
the stock firmware plays arp steps as plain flams.

## Faster knobs

Hold SHIFT while turning a knob to change values in bigger steps (8 times for 0-127 values, 10 times
for 0-255 like BPM). Bipolar values stop at their center on the way (DJ filter off, pan center, no
detune), lists keep single steps. The encoder is unchanged.

## LFOs on the whole unit

Set an LFO's target voice (`vce`) to `Prf` to modulate settings of the whole unit: the global sample
rate, the DJ filter cutoff or its resonance. The LFO swings around the knob position; when it targets
something else again, the DJ filter returns to its knob values. Saved in the kit; in the stock firmware
such an LFO is off.

## Pattern management

On the pattern load and save pages (LOAD/SAVE + PATTERN):

- The display shows the slot under the encoder as `[05] Name`. The encoder scrolls through all 64 slots
  and the step buttons follow its bank; its button works exactly like the step button of that slot.
- Lit step buttons show the slots that contain steps. The playing pattern blinks slowly, the pattern
  that plays next blinks fast until it takes over at the end of the current pattern.
- Patterns have names. Saving asks "Edit Name?" like kits do, and saving over another slot with steps
  asks for a second press first.

## Kits and patterns from other projects

"Change Project" (below kit 0 in the kit menus, above slot 1 on the pattern pages) lists the kits or
patterns of other projects.

- **A kit loaded from another project** replaces the current kit temporarily: nothing is written until
  you save it into a kit slot. A project save keeps the kit slot you had loaded before, the autosave
  leaves it out (so it isn't back after switching off), and loading another kit or a pattern change
  that loads its kit discards it. Before 1.3 a project save or the autosave could write it into the kit
  slot loaded before. Unsaved changes of a kit from the own project are still written into its slot by a
  project save, as in the stock firmware.
- **A pattern loaded from another project** replaces the playing pattern at the next pattern change (at
  once while the sequencer is stopped); only the pattern comes over, the kit stays. It plays like unsaved
  changes of the playing slot and is temporary too: nothing is written until you save it into a slot, a
  project save keeps the slot's saved pattern, the autosave leaves it out, and switching to another
  pattern discards it.
- **Saving into another project** works like saving into the own one (overwrite question, name dialog)
  and writes only that project's file. A pattern saved there points to its kit 1.

## Fixes

- **A voice could stay silent until a reboot.** With very high cutoff, resonance and filter drive, the
  filter of a voice can blow up. The stock firmware's reset for this was removed by the compiler, so the
  voice stayed silent. Kit and pattern changes made this likely, because parameters arrive one at a
  time.
- **Turning one knob could nudge another one by a step** (the ADC sampled too briefly).
- **The encoder needed an extra click when changing direction**, in every menu.
- **Note names** follow the usual convention now: MIDI note 0 is C-1, 60 is C4, 127 is G9 (stock: 0 was
  C 0 and the top octave showed `:`). Only the display changed.

## Also included

Everything from 1.2: the DJ filter, uninterrupted playback, freely assignable voice engines (SHIFT + KIT),
loading single voices and kits from any project, the limiter (switchable in the config menu), the safe
project save and the stock firmware fixes. Details:
[README](https://github.com/tunefish777/openelixir-02/blob/v1.3/README.md).

## Installing

1. Download `LXR_OpenElixir-02_V1.3.img` below.
2. Copy it to the top folder of the SD card and delete any other `LXR*.img` files there.
3. Switch the LXR-02 off, insert the card, hold the encoder button and switch it on. Keep holding
   until "LXR Updater" appears.
4. Wait for "Update OK!". The device restarts with the new firmware.

To go back, install the official firmware update from Erica Synths the same way. Kits and patterns saved
with OpenElixir-02 keep working there: slots with a different engine play with their stock engine, arp
steps play as flams and `Prf` LFOs are off.

The `.hex` and `.elf` files are for programming and debugging with an ST-Link; you don't need them for
a normal update.
